audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer said 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer read Karma/Karma/Karma/Karma/Galio/Karma/Galio, and the content whys[] were misaligned against their own rows — whys[2] (Level 3) described 'the instant he hits 6' and whys[3] (Levels 4-5) described him 'starting to use his ultimate'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart matches the content layer, and Galio's kit supports it: no engage until Justice Punch, an 825-range damage-over-time Q that never kills, a 275-range taunt, and a 180s ult that decides fights rather than lanes.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved onto the content values, and every why plus the misaligned whys[2] and whys[3] rewritten to describe the level they actually sit on.
sources: brief.enemyKit Galio Q range 825, W range 275, E cd 11/10/9/8/7

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why said 'No new ult... press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up' on the Level 6 row, and the ult itself was named 'Idol of Durand' in whys[2], spikes[1].text, mid and wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s and lands from 4000/4750/5500 range, shielding allies in the area and knocking up on impact. Idol of Durand is Galio's pre-rework ultimate name and does not exist in the current kit — Shield of Durand is his W.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the 4000-range, shield-and-knockup ult, and every Idol of Durand reference is replaced with Hero's Entrance.
sources: brief.enemyKit Galio R = Hero's Entrance, cd 180/160/140, range 4000/4750/5500
brief.enemyKit Galio W = Shield of Durand

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's headline defect: the page never named a single Galio ability beyond Justice Punch. breakdown.cooldowns also held no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and the brief's Colossal Smash auto-reset interaction was absent.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7s and is his only engage. Shield of Durand is 18/17/16/15/14s and taunts at 275 range, but it is a charged stance — Galio moves slowly while charging, which is the visible tell Karma needs since her Soul Shield speed is what walks her out of the radius. Colossal Smash empowers his next basic attack every few seconds for area damage, so the attack wind-up is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, tradeGood, tradeBad, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d and report[5].t now name Colossal Smash, Winds of War, Shield of Durand, Justice Punch and Hero's Entrance with their real numbers.
sources: brief.enemyKit Galio W cd/range and charge text
brief.enemyKit Galio P text and autoReset flag

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions asked for 'Galio can cut your retreat with Justice Punch (E) and you have no dash — hold Flash for the wall, not the damage.'
audit.why: Justice Punch carries a derived 'terrain' flag, but Riot's description is a step-back charge that knocks up the first champion hit — it creates no terrain. Per the standing rule I trusted the description and did not write the retreat-cutting claim. The flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire and is worth fixing upstream.

edits.before: The instant Galio hits level 6 you need to respect him — Idol of Durand can bail out a losing ally or flip a fight anywhere near the map, making him a serious threat in skirmishes even if his lane damage is still low. Once he finishes a tank-support item his passive shield and W taunt make him considerably tankier and harder to punish in an all-in, shrinking your kill windows further. Keep poking but don't expect to burst through his defenses solo — his value now comes from disruption rather than raw damage, so ward for his roams and play safer around skirmishes. This stretch starts favoring him as his utility comes online.
edits.after: The instant Galio hits level 6 you need to respect him — Hero's Entrance lands from 4000 range to shield a losing ally and knock up everyone around them, making him a serious threat in skirmishes even if his lane damage is still low. Once he finishes a tank item the Shield of Durand taunt at 275 makes him considerably harder to punish in an all-in, shrinking your kill windows further. Keep poking but don't expect to burst through him solo — his value is disruption rather than damage, so ward for his roams and play safer around skirmishes. This stretch starts favoring him as his utility comes online.

notes:
CHART: full layer said 'Skill' on all seven rows; content and the packet levelChart both read Karma/Karma/Karma/Karma/Galio/Karma/Galio. Full sides moved onto that, all seven whys rewritten. No paired win[N] edits — win[0..6] already hold the target values, so a pair would be before==after.

MISALIGNED whys[]: whys[2] sits on the Level 3 row but described 'the instant he hits 6', and whys[3] on Levels 4-5 described him using his ultimate. Both rewritten to describe the level they actually render under. Worth checking whether the same off-by-one exists on other Karma matchups.

FABRICATED ABILITY: 'Idol of Durand' appeared four times (whys[2], spikes[1].text, mid, wants.foe[1]). That is Galio's pre-rework ultimate; the current one is Hero's Entrance and Shield of Durand is his W. All four replaced.

PACKET DEFECT ADDRESSED: 'never names any of Galio's abilities'. Colossal Smash, Winds of War, Shield of Durand, Justice Punch and Hero's Entrance now all appear with real numbers.

DERIVED-FLAG MISFIRE: Justice Punch carries a 'terrain' flag and missingInteractions asked for a retreat-cutting line. Riot's text is a step-back charge that knocks up the first champion hit — no terrain. Claim not written.

SCOPE: two report[] edits only (report[0].t, report[5].t). report[1].t and report[3].t still carry the old winCon / tradeGood / tradeBad strings verbatim and will read stale.

UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Shield of Durand's taunt is reduced by tenacity, whether Karma's Q projectile is blocked by anything in Galio's kit, and whether the Hero's Entrance knockup can be avoided by being airborne on arrival. None are in Riot's text.
